cells.tense: The structure you built is doing its work, and the people inside it are getting back what they put in.
cells.act: accept what is offered for what you gave
cells.ask: When someone offers to take something off your hands, let them. Don't square it by nightfall. One exchange runs both ways and stays uneven a while.
cells.core:
You built a container and it's holding — the shape of the week, who covers what, where the lines fall. That's not small. Structure that keeps working after you stop tending it is the hard part, and you've got some of it. And the people inside it are getting back what they put in. Let that count as a fact, not a gap you haven't closed yet.

The next move is to accept. When someone offers to take something off your hands, let them, and don't square it before the day ends. Take one thing someone hands you and keep it. The fairness you've built is strong enough to hold a debt running in your favour for a while. Let it, and you'll have something to test the structure against.
cells.sheetLine: The structure holds, and the exchange still runs both ways.
cells.verb: holding what change produced, in a form that lasts
cells.place: in the part of life where you set the pattern and keep it

cells.tense: You're braced for a version of this that hasn't happened yet, and the structure is going up faster than the need for it.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Before the next rule or layer goes in, follow whatever feeling is pulling at you a little. A minute, no notebook. Then see if the addition still needs making.
cells.core:
There's a future version you're organising for — the one where it all goes wrong, where someone drops a ball, where the structure has to hold more than it does. So the rules get added, the layers go up, and the container gets tighter than the thing inside it needs.

Before the next rule goes in, pause on the feeling pulling at you and follow it a little — a minute, no notebook. The pull usually points at something real, and it doesn't need a rule to be met. What it needs is to be felt once, up close, without being turned into architecture. Then decide whether the structure still needs the addition.
cells.sheetLine: You're building for a future that hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door you already walked through, and the shape of this thing was decided back there.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Hold one direction you already chose for this structure when something pushes at it. Don't relitigate. Say the heading again, quietly, and don't move it.
cells.core:
The structure is here, but you're not quite in it. You set it up, and now you stand at the edge looking back at the decision that made it, as though the choice is still open and you're still the one who has to make it. The container functions. The founding of it is where you live.

Take one direction you already chose for this thing — a line you drew, a shape you settled on — and hold it when something pushes. Not relitigate it: hold it. Say the heading again, quietly, and don't move it. Defending a chosen direction is how momentum comes back to a seat that's running on empty. You don't need to feel certain to keep the heading. You just need to keep it.

cells.tense: You're running the structure without calling it yours, and the room already knows who's holding it.
cells.act: let the structure act instead of announcing it
cells.ask: Decide the shape of the next thing and carry it through the same day, no announcement. Do it once and notice you did it.
cells.core:
There's a way things get organised around you — the group finds its shape, the mess becomes workable, someone finally says what the plan is, and it's usually you. You'd call it the room sorting itself out. But the room is looking at you when it does. The authority is on the ground, operating, and the hand on it is not being claimed.

Decide the shape of the next thing and move the same day, without announcing that you've decided. No framing, no preamble. Just the call, carried through. The point isn't the decision. The point is that one moment later you'll know you did it — and that's the acknowledgment. The structure doesn't need a speech. It needs its author to notice the pen was in their hand.
cells.sheetLine: The structure is yours. You'd say it sorted itself.
cells.verb: holding what change produced, in a form that lasts
cells.place: in the part of life where you set the pattern and keep it
